title: Add MP4 compatibility library mode
summary: Adds backend-owned MP4 compatibility mode metadata and policy, exposes it as a per-library WebView compatibility action, and updates Python and PowerShell FFmpeg planning paths to strip MP4-incompatible media features.
reason: MP4 has stricter media-container limits than MKV. Operators need MP4 to be an explicit lossy compatibility mode with warnings and atomic overrides instead of a plain container dropdown choice.
behavior_before: MKV remained the default, but selecting MP4 behaved primarily like a container value. Audio, subtitle, attachment, and metadata constraints were not consistently forced or warned across backend preview, PowerShell FFmpeg construction, and the library settings UI.
behavior_after: MKV remains the default. MP4 compatibility can be applied per library as an explicit preset that forces MP4, H.264/H.265-compatible video policy, one preferred-language EAC3 audio track, external-SRT-only subtitle posture, no embedded subtitles or attachments/fonts, stripped metadata/chapters, and faststart muxing.
